title: Quick incident triage map — night shift cheat
content:
Purpose: 30–60s triage checklist for the person grabbing the pager. Not a full runbook — absolute minimum to stabilize and hand to next shift. Treat as notes-to-self: quick commands, common fingerprints, escalation pointers, and temporary mitigations.

Top-line first actions (first 5 minutes)
- Console: open redwood-console -> incidents -> active. Note incident ID and affected model/route.
- Check PagerDuty / Slack (SRE Night rotation) for any automatic annotations.
- Scope: is this one route/one model or cluster-wide? If >3 routes showing latency errors, assume infra-level.

Quick signals to read (order matters)
1) redwood-console incident detail (latency percentiles, error class)
2) kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | grep -E "Crash|Evicted|OOM|Error"
3) journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 400 --no-pager | grep -E "CUDA|OOM|KV cache miss|failed to allocate|segfault|Assertion"
4) curl -sS https://internal-metrics.redwood.local/health | jq '.' (if accessible)

Common fingerprints + quick likely cause
- High p95/p99 token latency, isolated to a few pods: possible slow disk or node CPU contention. Check node metrics (CPU steal, iowait).
- Rapid 5xx spike across all regions for a model: model rollout bug or cache priming failure -> fallback policy should route to stable variant.
- CrashLoopBackOff for serving-runtime pods: check OOM and GPU memory logs. Likely memory leak or oversized batch/seq config.
- Authentication/503 from upstream (model store or KMS): check KMS logs and model download errors in runtime logs.

First-stop remediations (fast, reversible)
- If one deployment has bad rollout: rollback to previous revision (kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n redwood-serving) and mark incident as "rollback attempted".
- If GPU OOM: scale down concurrency on that node/pod (patch deployment with lower THREADS/BATCH_SIZE env) or cordon node temporarily (kubectl cordon <node>) and drain if necessary.
- If KV cache thrash causing latency: purge prefix cache for the hot route (temporary) and enable cache-only mode by setting route policy -> cache_on=false in console.
- If model download errors: toggle fallback policy to stable variant (redwood route update --route <route> --fallback stable-variant).
- If autoscaler not adding pods and queue backpressure high: check HPA metrics, then manually scale (kubectl scale deployment/<name> --replicas=<n> -n redwood-serving) to buy time.

Useful commands (copy-paste ready)
- Pods + status: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide | grep -v Running
- Recent runtime errors: journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 500 | tail -n 200
- Model fetch errors: grep -i "download failed" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | tail -n 200
- Check Redis cache: redis-cli -h redis-main -p 6379 INFO stats | egrep "keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses|used_memory"
- Rollback deployment: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<deployment> -n redwood-serving && kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment> -n redwood-serving
- Temporarily scale: kubectl scale deployment/<deployment> --replicas=3 -n redwood-serving
- Check node GPU memory: ssh ops@node-xx 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv'

Escalation matrix (who to ping)
- If model inference errors (bad outputs/quality regressions) -> ping Applied ML on Slack @maya.tm + open INFR ticket.
- If platform-level outage (>=3 routes or cross-region) -> alert SRE leads: Ethan (pager), then Director on-call. Use PD-escalation policy.
- If security-related (KMS, credential exposure) -> stop, escalate to Security (sec-oncall@redwood) and do NOT restart services without approval.

Short-lived alternatives (temporary toggles)
- Shift traffic to hosted pool: use console routing -> set policy to prefer hosted for affected route (manual override).
- Reduce batch sizes globally for a model: patch configmap redwood-model-config -> decrease default_batch_size. This is a blunt lever — expect throughput drop.
- Disable background evals: POST to /ops/evals/disable for the specific model to reduce resource pressure.

Hand-off checklist for the next on-call
- Paste incident IDs + short cause hypothesis + actions taken (rollbacks, manual scales, cache purges).
- Attach timeline: when alerts fired, when we scaled/rolled back, when spikes subsided.
- List any escalations (who was paged and when) and expected follow-ups (PRs, config changes).
- Mark any TODOs: e.g., "recreate replica in eu-west-1", "investigate model memory leak with @ethan".

Notes to self / rough todos (post-incident follow-ups)
- Add a specific alert for KV cache miss rate (current alert only tracks Redis down).
- Add a short runbook entry for the model reroute CLI (command snippets).
- Follow up on PR #987 (serving-runtime memory allocations) — add memprofile in night builds.

Reminders (non-urgent)
- Keep an eye on Dedicated pools: they sometimes show capacity plateau even though nodes appear healthy; check node labels for 'reserved' flags.
- For private deployments, KMS latency can be deceptive; if model fetches fail, test KMS separately before rolling back.

Common false positives
- Short p99 blips that correlate with a single long-running request (10s+): not an automatic paging signal unless repeatable.
- Brief host-level CPU spike immediately after a large batch job: often harmless if stability resumes in 2–3 minutes.

Quick references (one-liners)
- Incident playbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Playbooks
- PD schedule: https://pagerduty.com/orgs/redwood/schedules/SRE-Night

If you take this pager: put a brief note in #sre-oncall (time + 1 line hypothesis). Saves the next person 5–10 minutes.

Unresolved questions to surface in postmortem:
- Was fallback variant quality-signed? (check QA tags on model in console)
- Did autoscaler misreport CPU because of container QoS class? (look at kubelet logs)

End-of-shift handover line (copy this into Slack on transfer):
- "Taking over SRE pager at <time>. Active incidents: <list IDs>. Hypothesis: <short>. Actions: <rolled back/decreased-batch/scaled>. Next: <what to watch>."

Last note: this is intentionally terse. If you need more than what's here in first 10 minutes, escalate and ask for help — we don't want to tinker when system is not stable.
